title: Adaptive Prometheus/OTel Relay for Inference KPIs with Span-Aware Label Stitching
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Build an intermediary relay component that accepts both Prometheus pulls/pushes and OTLP metric streams, normalizes inference-specific KPIs (per-request latency, model_token_count, kv_cache_hits, cold_start_flag), and emits tenant-scoped Prometheus metrics with stitched labels derived from trace-span hooks. The relay should: (1) preserve exemplar/span IDs for high-cardinality tracing linkability, (2) perform tenant-aware relabeling to canonicalize model and route labels, (3) apply histogram bucketing compatible with existing dashboard aggregates, and (4) provide an admission buffer for edge/backfilled telemetry to prevent downstream overload.
acceptance_criteria: Relay accepts OTLP/gRPC and Prometheus remote_write inputs and forwards canonicalized Prometheus remote_write to metrics ingestion layer
Span ID exemplars are propagated for >95% of request-latency metrics when provided by runtime sidecars
Tenant relabeling rules map legacy labels (model_name, route) to canonical (model_id, route_id) for 100% of instrumented routes used in dedicated and hosted clusters
Histogram buckets match telemetry-contract v2 (see links) and dashboards show no regression in 99th percentile latency compared to baseline
Relay sustains 20k reqs/sec with <200ms processing p50 on standard instance and backpressure behavior documented
Integration tests covering wire format translation, label stitching, exemplar propagation, and schema evolution pass in CI
design_decisions: Use a single binary with modular input adapters (OTLP, Prometheus remote_write) and a shared normalization pipeline to avoid divergent behavior between paths
Perform label stitching using trace-span tag precedence: span.resource.model_id > metric.labels.model_name > header.model_alias
Emit Prometheus remote_write batches to existing metric gateway; avoid direct TSDB writes in this iteration
Implement exemplar propagation by copying tracing.span_id into exemplar.trace_id field to preserve trace-metric linkage for downstream SLI tooling
tradeoffs: Normalization at the relay increases processing latency slightly but centralizes contract enforcement — chosen to reduce downstream schema drift
Keeping exemplar propagation best-effort avoids blocking metrics that lack span context, but means some metrics will be unlinkable
Opted for remote_write output to leverage existing HA and rollups; adds one more hop vs direct ingestion which could reduce end-to-end latency
implementation_plan: Week 1: scaffold relay binary and input adapters (OTLP/gRPC receiver, Prometheus remote_write receiver), add simple passthrough path
Week 2: implement label canonicalizer, tenant mapping store (in-memory with snapshot reload), and histogram bucket mapper
Week 3: add exemplar/span extraction & propagation, integrate with trace hooks from sidecars (protocol documented), and add slow-path buffering/backpressure
Week 4: e2e integration tests, performance tuning (batch sizes, goroutine limits), and internal dogfood on staging with two tenants
Week 5: rollout plan execution and monitoring cutover; deprecate legacy ingest adapters in a future follow-up
rollout_plan: Canary deploy to telemetry-staging with traffic from non-production tenants only
Enable exemplar propagation flag off by default; flip for two low-risk tenants and validate dashboards
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% traffic over 48h windows with rollback if error budget consumed
Remove compatibility toggle after 2 weeks of stable metrics and no contract violations reported
testing_plan: Unit tests for label canonicalizer and histogram mapper
Integration tests: OTLP-in -> relay -> metrics-gateway (mock) asserting label/output equivalence
Load tests replicating tenant-mixed traffic (hot tenants + small tenants) to validate backpressure and tenant fairness
Chaos tests: introduce delayed spans and missing labels to ensure robust best-effort behavior
Golden file tests for remote_write payloads to detect accidental schema changes
monitoring_and_alerting: Relay internal metrics: input_rate, output_rate, processing_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, buffer_size, drop_count
DDD alerts: processing_latency_p95 > 1s for 10m, drop_count > 10/min sustained, exemplar_loss_rate > 20%
Dashboards: per-tenant throughput/latency with exemplar-linked traces, migration diff dashboard to compare old vs new ingestion for critical KPIs
Runbook: quick rollback steps, how to re-enable legacy adapter, and steps to triage exemplar mismatches
